sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Damin-i-koh**: The specific territory in the Rajmahal Hills (Jharkhand/Bihar) demarcated by the British for Santhal settlement, which later became the epicenter of the rebellion.
• **Dikus**: The derogatory term used by Santhals for outsiders, including moneylenders (mahajans), traders, and colonial officials who exploited them through usury and land alienation.
• **Hul**: The Santhal term for 'rebellion' or 'liberation movement', signifying a divine-sanctioned struggle against oppression.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The rebellion was triggered by the 'Triple Oppression' of the Zamindari system, the police-court nexus, and the usurious interest rates of moneylenders.

items.definition: A special administrative unit created post-1855 to provide legal protection to Santhals, marking a shift in British policy from total neglect to paternalistic control.
The practice of charging exorbitant interest rates (often 50-500%) by moneylenders, which trapped Santhals in perpetual debt-bondage.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Divine Legitimacy**: Sidhu and Kanhu claimed to have received 'Thakurs' (divine) orders to revolt, mobilizing thousands through religious fervor.
• **Guerrilla Tactics**: Use of bows, arrows, and axes against British muskets, showcasing the asymmetry of the conflict.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of modern weaponry and coordination with other regional uprisings (e.g., 1857 Revolt).
• **Solutions**: Post-rebellion, the British adopted the 'Non-Regulation' system to pacify the region.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-C-B-B' (The Four Brothers).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, and Bhairav were the four brothers who led the rebellion.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Santhal Rebellion (1855) with the Munda Ulgulan (1899). Remember: Santhal = Sidhu/Kanhu; Munda = Birsa Munda.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Resistance' to describe the Santhal Hul, highlighting the agency of marginalized groups against colonial hegemony.

keyTakeaways: The Santhal Rebellion was a reaction to the failure of the Permanent Settlement to protect tribal land rights.
It forced the British to recognize the need for special administrative status for tribal areas (Santhal Parganas).
It serves as a precursor to the 1857 revolt, highlighting the widespread discontent against British economic policies.
